title: Minimum spanning tree
learn: Prim's (heap) vs Kruskal's (sort + DSU), what an MST is used for
hook: Min Cost to Connect All Points is the standard MST interview question. Kruskal and Prim are also the cleanest examples of greedy algorithms that are provably correct.

explain.prompt: Explain what a minimum spanning tree is and how Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms build one.
keyPoints: an MST connects all V nodes with V − 1 edges of minimum total weight and no cycles
Kruskal: sort edges by weight, add each edge unless its endpoints are already connected (union-find)
Prim: grow one tree, always adding the cheapest edge that leaves it (min-heap)
Kruskal O(E log E); Prim O(E log V), or O(V²) with an array for dense graphs like all pairs of points
an MST minimises the total, not the path between two specific nodes
